business_problem: Scaleway needed a secure, scalable AI infrastructure that would let European customers train large models inside the EU while meeting data-sovereignty, privacy, and efficiency requirements.
solution_summary: Scaleway assembled its sovereign AI cloud around the Nabu supercomputer so European customers could train frontier models inside the EU without handing data control to non-European hyperscalers. The environment is built from 127 NVIDIA DGX H100 systems and 1,016 NVIDIA H100 Tensor Core GPUs, with NVIDIA NVLink handling intra-node bandwidth and Quantum-2 InfiniBand providing low-latency cluster communication. Hosted in Scaleway's DC5 data center in Paris, the platform gives customers a managed environment for training LLMs and other transformer workloads while staying aligned with GDPR and local data-sovereignty requirements. Scaleway used the same stack to support projects such as Mistral AI's Mixtral and Kyutai's Moshi, while its smaller Jero system extends the model to additional workloads. Energy-efficient data-center cooling reduces electricity and water usage, so the architecture pairs scale-out AI training with compliance and sustainability goals.

data_flow: Customer model-training jobs are submitted into Scaleway's DGX-based cloud, GPUs and NVLink handle node-level training, Quantum-2 InfiniBand connects the cluster for distributed runs, and completed models remain inside EU-hosted infrastructure for downstream customer use.
business_outcome: Scaleway stood up its Nabu supercomputer in two months, gave European AI companies a sovereign alternative for large-model training, and paired that scale with GDPR-aligned hosting and lower-power, lower-water data-center operations.

evidence_quotes: The company built the Nabuchodonosor 2023 AI supercomputer-known as Nabu-in just two months.

Powered by 1,016 NVIDIA H100 Tensor Core GPUs and 127 NVIDIA DGX H100 systems, Nabu offers European businesses access to a turnkey solution capable of supporting the most demanding machine learning tasks.
Its AI infrastructure complies with stringent data protection laws, like the EU's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).
DC5 uses advanced adiabatic cooling systems, reducing electricity consumption by 30-40% and using 9-10X less water than traditional data centers.
